Theme 046 · Metaphor concepts

Conservator's UV Lamp

Your dashboards hang like paintings in a conservation studio: in normal light they look flawless. Acme Pulse is a slow UV lamp; wherever its pool passes, hidden layers fluoresce and one figure glows coral like overpaint. The conservator, a human, writes the condition report and makes the call.

readability ●●○trust ●●●effort med
1 · HOOK0:00–0:08

A slow dolly left to right along the gallery wall; every frame looks perfect in warm light. On the downbeat before the drop the museum label's "last inspected: never" types in and the room lights click off.

2 · REVEAL0:08 (drop)

Darkness; the UV wand clicks on at the top and its violet pool slides down onto the wall. On the drop the mark and "Acme Pulse" fluoresce 0→1 behind a glow filter, as if they had always been painted there.

3 · PROOF MOMENT0:12–0:32

The UV pool drifts left to right across the chart along a bezier (2.5 s, power1.inOut); the smooth "painted" line fluoresces into the real one, which drops in coral after 09:42. The brass loupe punches in on the downbeat (back.out) and the condition report writes its failing line; the conservator taps "Roll back".

4 · CTA0:36–0:45

Room lights fade back up to warm; the camera settles on one framed work, the Acme lockup, under a gallery spot. The tagline lands on beat 1, the museum label slides in from the right on beat 3, and the button lands on the final downbeat.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Framed dashboard — gilt frame, mat and a chart as the artwork, with a museum label card.
  • UV pool — radial violet mask carried by a handheld wand; the agent itself.
  • Fluorescent layer — the real data under the "painted" surface, teal-glowing, coral where it disagrees.
  • Brass loupe — circle clip at 2.5× that isolates the anomaly figure.
  • Condition report — mono checklist card; the failing line carries the anomaly and deploy.
  • Conservator's decision — Roll back / Acknowledge; the human signs the report.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Lamp pass — mask follows a bezier path over 2.5 s (five beats at 120 BPM), power1.inOut, arriving on the anomaly exactly on a downbeat.
  • Fluoresce — revealed layer 0→1 behind a glow filter in 0.3 s; afterglow fades over 0.8 s once the lamp moves on.
  • Loupe punch-in — circle scales 0→1 with back.out(1.7) in 0.35 s on the snare; the report line types in with steps() over the next bar.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

"Looks fine on the surface, wrong underneath" is exactly the anomaly problem, and conservation science makes the hidden layer tangible with a warm, trustworthy museum tone. Risk: glow can tip into sci-fi; keep the paper warm and the museum restrained.

Adapt to your product: Hang your own report, invoice or config as the artwork and let the UV layer show what your product checks underneath; the condition report becomes your finding list.

References: Cyanilux, UV light and invisible ink shader · D&AD 2023, Data Auction (making the invisible physical)
